mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office at the seat of the company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention route only: obtain official Certified Corporate Registration Extract from the Korean registry; notarize any required copy before a Korean notary public; obtain an Apostille Certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular legalization is not applicable and must not be chained with the apostille because both routes are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea and the Supreme Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention route only: request official tax clearance and corporate existence certificate from the National Tax Service and the court registry; notarize the certificate; obtain Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. No consular legalization step may be added because Korea is a contracting party to the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public appointed under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute and notarize the board resolution or power of attorney before a Korean notary; obtain a MOFA Apostille Certificate certified under the Convention of 5 October 1961; do not combine with consular legalization for use in any other Apostille contracting state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or registry office certifying the original Korean-language Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticate the Articles of Association through notarial certification of the Korean-language instrument; apply to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for an Apostille Certificate; consular legalization may not be used in addition to the apostille, as the two are parallel and alternative channels.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the initial USD/KRW operating account, with corroborating countersignature by the Korean receiving bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention route only: issue the bank reference letter on bank letterhead; have the bank officer's signature notarized; obtain an Apostille Certificate from the competent authority of the bank's jurisdiction or from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea if issued by a Korean bank. Consular legalization is not applicable for Apostille member states and may not be appended.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the KYC officer must screen all natural persons against the KoFIU specified financial transaction information database, the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic designations maintained by the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance. PEP status must be independently verified using open-source evidence, corporate registers, and digital identity verification. Repeat the full screening cycle every 30 days for every UBO, and document any hit, false positive, or name-matched result with supporting metadata before filing the UBO report with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Commercial Registration Information Network (Hoopis) and the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (iREG), operated by the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be registered in Hangul. A foreign trade name or brand must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul through the four-tier registration convention: (1) distinctive primary trademark or trade name, (2) objective statement of business purpose, (3) transliterated foreign brand segment where applicable, and (4) mandatory limited-liability suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'. An additional English or romanized name may be registered for banking and invoicing convenience, but the controlling legal name on the Certificate of Incorporation remains the Hangul name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a name-rejection notice, the applicant must file a written request for re-examination with the registry officer of the relevant district court, annexing a side-by-side name comparison table, the Korean language translation, and the complete notarized and apostilled instrument package. If re-examination is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Supreme Court of Korea under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of the denial. The appeal must cite Commercial Act Article 19, Korean name-clearance review standards, and the absence of confusing similarity, and may request an oral hearing only upon a showing of arbitrary discrimination or manifest registry error.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the principal registered office for a marine insurance surveyor entity in South Korea. The National Tax Service and domestic banks reject a virtual address for this industry because a marine claims inspection surveyor must maintain an actual fixed place of business for storing calibrated survey instruments, receiving registered tax and maritime correspondence, producing client claim files on short notice, and accommodating unannounced inspection visits. Banks performing UBO and AML due diligence will also require a physical lease, employee presence indicators, and surveyor license records before opening a corporate account or approving underwriter wire and Wise payment rails.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) current business registration certificate displayed; (2) exterior signboard and physical lock-and-key office control; (3) employment insurance and industrial accident insurance records; (4) original marine claims survey reports; (5) marine surveyor licenses and professional indemnity insurance certificates; (6) calibration records for vessel hull and cargo survey equipment; (7) client claim files and inspection appointment logs; (8) IT and communication systems; (9) VAT tax invoices and corporate tax records; (10) UBO and compliance register. Quantified risk: for a licensed, low-risk marine surveyor company, the probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the National Tax Service or municipal tax office is assessed between 40% and 55% during the first year of operation, rising to 65% if the company claims maritime service tax incentives or receives foreign-underwriter revenue through remittance channels.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1241, as amended), especially Articles 287-2 through 287-67 concerning Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability companies) and the general provisions on incorporation and board of directors under Articles 330 and 388-399
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court for the registered office district, operating under the Supreme Court Registration Authority of the Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Registration (Registry Form 2) before the competent district court; upon approval, the certified corporate register extract serves as the certificate of incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa, and no blocked escrow deposit is mandatory prior to formation. However, all subscribed contributions must be fully paid in before the registration application is filed, and the payment must be evidenced by a deposit certificate or capital contribution receipt issued by a licensed Korean bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF FIRST MEETING OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR_YUHANGHOESA (Yuhan Hoesa, Ltd.). The undersigned directors of KR_YUHANGHOESA (the 'Company'), a Yuhan Hoesa incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (the 'Act'), acting as the duly appointed initial directors, hereby record the following resolutions adopted at the first meeting of the board of directors. WHEREAS the Company has been subscribed to, and all paid-up capital has been deposited in an escrow account with a banking corporation as required under the Act; NOW, THEREFORE, the board unanimously resolves as follows: 1. Share Capital Subscription and Allotment: The board accepts the reported capital subscription of the Company, endorses the receipt of actual payment of subscription amounts, authorizes the representative director to issue the relevant capital contribution certificates, and directs that the register of shareholders be prepared, completed and kept at the registered office. 2. Registered Office: The board establishes the registered office at the location described in the articles of incorporation and authorizes the execution of a lease for the registered office premises, the installation of the company name sign, and the registration of the office with the competent registry officer. 3. Banking Arrangements: The board approves the opening of corporate bank accounts at a licensed Korean bank; authorizes the representative director and one additional designated director as authorised signatories; mandates that all negotiable instruments, checks, foreign exchange transactions and wire transfers bear the signatures of the two authorised signatories unless otherwise specified in a future resolution; and directs that all banking service agreements be executed under seal. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments: The board appoints [Name] as representative director, [Name] as registered director, and [Name] as statutory auditor if required by the Act. The representative director is fully empowered to act for the Company, to sign notices, filings and contracts, and to delegate to the auditor the duty of supervising management. 5. Licenses and Tax Filings: The board instructs the representative director to register the Company with the National Tax Service, obtain a business registration certificate, file the VAT registration under the VAT Act, and pursue all licenses required to conduct marine cargo inspection and insurance claims surveying services, including any necessary registration as a licensed damage appraiser pursuant to the Insurance Business Act. The board also confirms that all acts performed in furthering incorporation prior to this meeting, including disbursements, are ratified by this resolution. There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean notary or law office with notarial powers, under the supervision of the Korea Notary Association and the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal representative must execute the Korean-language articles of incorporation in the presence of a notary public. Under the Commercial Act and Notarial Deeds Act, the notary verifies the identities of the incorporators and certifies that the object and provisions are lawful. The articles must set forth (i) corporate name, (ii) object clause, (iii) registered office address, (iv) fully-paid capital amount, (v) number of units into which the contribution is divided and the amount of contribution per unit, (vi) method of delivering consideration, and (vii) appointment of the first directors. The notary produces a certified duplicate to be submitted to the registration court. All corporate signatures and seals must be attested in the notary office, and the process is completed on the same day if documents are pre-drafted.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation in Korean
Passport or national ID and alien registration card of each incorporator/director
Power of attorney if submitted through an agent
Proof of business address intention such as a draft lease summary
Corporate seal specimen and personal seal certificates of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries any unlawful provision or incomplete purpose clause, the incorporators must amend the articles and resubmit within three business days; a formal written correction notice is issued and an expedited re-notarization can be obtained on the next business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office address, operating under the Supreme Court Registration Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registration application must be submitted on the official company registration form for a limited liability company, accompanied by the notarized articles, capital contribution payment certificate, first board resolution, confirmation that the representative director has not been disqualified, corporate seal certificate, and a power of attorney. The registry court reviews the compliance of the company name, purpose clause, capital subscription and officer appointments. After payment of the registration fee through court fee stamps, the registrar issues a certified extract from the corporate register proving legal personality. The entire filing can be made at the court window or through the electronic registration system of the Supreme Court.
required_dossiers: Notarized articles of incorporation
Capital contribution payment certificate or escrow deposit certificate
Certified copy of the first board resolution
Corporate seal certificate
Certificate of domicile or lease contract for registered office
Personal seal certificates and identity cards of directors
Power of attorney authorizing filing agent
Application form for corporation registration
Receipt of court fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplemental notice requiring corrections, the Company must resolve the defects within two weeks of the notice and resubmit the amended form; a formal objection may be filed if the registrar refuses registration, and an appeal to the Supreme Court Registration Division is available within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, local district tax office at the location of the business place, via the Home Tax Service portal at hometax.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the representative director must file a business registration application with the local tax office within 20 days of the corporate registration date. This registration creates the VAT business identification number and forms the legal basis for issuing electronic tax invoices, filing corporate income tax, and executing foreign currency transactions. The application must list the corporate name, business scope codes, corporate registration number, business premises, representative information and separate business places. For a marine insurance surveyor service under ISIC 5222, the object clause specifying marine cargo inspection and damage survey must be included. The tax office issues the business registration certificate and assigns a legal and VAT registration number.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration extract
Corporate seal certificate and personal seal certificates of representative
Lease agreement or proof of ownership of the business premises
Articles of incorporation copy
Application form for business registration under VAT Act Article 5
Copy of representative director and staff identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends the application due to mismatch of business premises or missing documentation, an additional submission of the paid-in capital report and lease deposit ledger shall resolve the query; if revocation of approval is threatened, the Company may file an administrative objection under the Framework Act on National Taxes within 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational KYC and Professional License Registration for Marine Survey and Claims Adjustment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (Insurance Business Act section) and/or Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Maritime Industry and Logistics Bureau, depending on whether the Company is acting as a loss adjuster for insurers or as a port marine surveyor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Since marine insurance survey services are regulated under the Insurance Business Act for loss adjusting activities, the representative must review whether the surveyor qualifies as a damage appraiser. If the Company inspects and reports on vessel hull damage, cargo damage, or insurance claims, a written certification of license eligibility must be submitted to the Financial Supervisory Service. Alternatively, if the Company conducts port-based physical inspections, a marine surveyor business registration with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries may be needed. The process includes submission of the business plan, professional qualification certificates, proof of office facilities, professional liability insurance, and the Company's compliance with financial soundness standards. A local KYC and anti-money laundering brief must be filed at the chosen payment counterparty bank due to the low-risk insurance underwriting wire transactions.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate
Corporate registration extract
Marine surveyor qualification certificates or professional membership credentials
Professional liability insurance policy certificate
Certified copy of office lease and facility layout
Business plan describing survey methodology and safety compliance
Proof of decennial professional education or continuing education
Company bank account certificate and authorized signatory list
AML/KYC self-assessment form for the payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is queried, the Company must submit supplemental explanatory documents to the respective financial or maritime regulator within 10 business days. If the registration is rejected, an administrative appeal can be filed with the Financial Services Commission or the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries' administrative appeals review committee.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax System electronic portal (hometax.go.kr), with customs-side processing via the Korea Customs Service (KCS) UNI-PASS system
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing or owning a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) in Korea: (1) complete corporate registration under the Korean Commercial Act at the competent registry and, where applicable, file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; (2) apply for business registration at the district tax office with jurisdiction over the domestic place of business; execute the statutory business registration application under the Framework Act on National Taxes; (3) submit the corporate articles of incorporation, certificate of corporate registration, proof of local establishment or place of business, identity documents of the statutory representative, and any foreign investment registration certificate or equity subscription evidence; (4) the NTS shall issue the 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN), which is the unified identifier for Corporate Tax, Value-Added Tax, withholdings, and other national tax filings; (5) for a foreign enterprise with no Korean place of business that nevertheless supplies taxable services in Korea, a simplified VAT registration under the Value-Added Tax Act must be made through a statutory tax representative, with a separately assigned foreign business registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for a Yuhan Hoesa: no check-the-box or passthrough election is available under Korean tax law. A Yuhan Hoesa is a resident domestic corporation taxable on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Act. The Korean group tax consolidation regime under the Corporate Income Tax Act is available only to qualifying Korean corporate groups and is not a passthrough election; capital gains, income, and losses remain recognised at entity level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa: VAT registration is mandatory from commencement of business under Article 5 of the Value-Added Tax Act, irrespective of anticipated turnover. For a foreign non-resident supplier of electronic services without a Korean place of business, a simplified registration obligation applies, with an annual sales threshold of KRW 30,000,000 for mandatory registration; this electronic-services rule is not relevant to a domestic marine insurance surveying company.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under the Korean electronic tax invoice regime, all VAT-registered businesses must issue Electronic Tax Invoices through the NTS HomeTax system for taxable supplies to other registered businesses, and transmit the invoice data to the NTS no later than the day following the statutory time of supply. Since 2021 the e-tax invoice mandate applies regardless of the supplier’s annual turnover. There is no physical fiscal stamp or Latin American style real-time fiscal clearance API; the anti-fraud control is effected through the NTS’s central e-tax invoice database and data matching. For retail cash sales, businesses must operate the cash receipt system, issuing cash receipts and transmitting transaction data to the NTS to preserve input tax credits for consumers and suppress hidden turnover.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rate eligibility is governed by Article 20 of the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree. Exports of goods qualify when the goods are delivered overseas or under customs export procedures. Services qualify for 0% VAT when performed outside Korea, or when rendered in Korea to a non-resident recipient in consideration of foreign currency and the service is actually used or consumed overseas. For the marine insurance surveying scope, zero-rating requires the services to be supplied to a foreign underwriter or principal, the contractual consideration to be received in foreign exchange, and the survey work to be evidenced as related to export-bound cargo, ocean-going vessels, or international marine transportation. Domestic survey services for Korean-resident principals are taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (KCS UNI-PASS export filing with export declaration number and validation result; the Korean statutory equivalent of an export bill of entry, applicable to goods movements)
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list identifying the supplier, recipient, export cargo, vessel, and stated zero-rated supply value
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical transportation of the goods out of Korea

Certificate of receipt of foreign currency issued by a foreign exchange bank (Korean statutory equivalent of an inward remittance certificate), documenting the inward remittance or foreign currency purchase supporting the export service proceeds

Marine survey report, vessel particulars, cargo damage documentation, and the insurance contract or engagement letter demonstrating that the recipient is a non-resident underwriter and that the claim inspection service was performed in connection with export/international marine insurance risk
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may retrospectively assess the 10% VAT with penalty taxes where a zero-rated export claim is unsupported, the required customs or foreign-exchange documents are missing, or the export proceeds are not collected within the statutory repatriation period of 180 days, unless an extension is approved by the foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Penalty tax exposure includes understatement and non-payment penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes, with aggravated penalties for deliberate concealment or the use of false tax invoices. In fraud or evasion cases, the taxpayer is subject to criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment, fines, and mandatory recovery of any VAT refund together with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (the central bank), with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign exchange control authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Korea Customs Service supervises trade settlement reporting and the Foreign Exchange Information Network is the electronic reporting gateway
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a market-determined foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decrees. The Korean won is freely convertible for current-account items such as marine insurance surveying fees, vessel hull and cargo damage inspection reimbursements, royalties, and professional fees, but every inward or outward remittance must be declared through a resident foreign exchange bank using standard transaction codes. Capital-account transactions are more structured: a foreign shareholder injecting equity into the Korean LLC, or the LLC extending or repaying shareholder loans, must first file a foreign investment notification or capital transaction declaration, after which the bank can lawfully convert the inbound currency into KRW. There is no statutory surrender quota applicable to service export proceeds, but the bank must verify the underlying contract, invoice, and business relationship to prevent disguised financing flows. Profit remittance from the LLC to an overseas shareholder is permitted on current-account grounds once distributable reserves are proven by audited financial statements, a board resolution is passed, and applicable Korean corporate tax and withholding obligations have been settled. Offshore KRW clearing is limited: the onshore market is ring-fenced, and non-resident access generally occurs through non-deliverable forwards rather than free third-country KRW settlement. Overall convertibility is high for genuine trade and service flows, but banks will require documentary substance and will reject speculative or undocumented capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Korea Customs Service settlement guidelines, general merchandise export proceeds must be received by a Korean foreign exchange bank within 15 months from the export declaration date unless the settlement term is extended due to letter-of-credit, project, or ship-construction conditions. Marine insurance surveying receipts are service-export earnings; they must be collected on the invoice due date, which the Korean bank will encode in the Foreign Exchange Information Network as a current-account service receipt. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0 percent for ordinary export and service receipts. South Korea does not impose a forced surrender requirement; a resident company may keep foreign currency in a licensed foreign exchange bank deposit account, convert to KRW at market rates, or use it for permitted external payments, but the funds must enter the republic through a designated Korean bank and remain traceable through SWIFT and Foreign Exchange Information Network reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms, including Wise, are not licensed banks or registered foreign exchange businesses under the Korean Banking Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. A Korean-resident LLC cannot lawfully rely on such an EMI for inbound equity subscription, marine insurance claim settlements, or trade disbursements because all capital-account and current-account foreign exchange transactions must be routed through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank. For the LLC, using Wise as a treasury rail would expose the client to unregistered money transmission risk and will cause a Korean relationship bank to refuse onboarding. The entity should use only SWIFT MT103 transfers from the licensed bank accounts of foreign underwriters, shipowners, and reinsurers; Wise may be relevant only for personal or non-corporate small-value scenarios and should not appear as a corporate treasury counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in branch is generally mandatory at first onboarding for a Korean LLC owned by non-residents. At least one statutory director or an authorised local officer holding a notarised and apostilled power of attorney must appear for the compliance interview because the Act on Reporting and Use of Financial Transaction Information requires an enhanced verification process for non-face-to-face corporate customers. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a standard right, although a few tier-one banks may consider a hybrid process after an initial physical visit, notarised corporate seal registration, and a documented board resolution. The bank must inspect original corporate seals, signature mandates, and beneficial ownership declarations before issuing the operating account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The LLC is newly registered with zero trading history and 100 percent non-resident ownership, so the bank may suspect shell or nominee formation and fail the beneficial ownership check.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and articles of association; original Korean business registration certificate; shareholder register and UBO declaration; certified passports of all directors and ultimate owners; bank statements and source-of-wealth report for each equity contributor; corporate seal registration certificate; 12-month business plan with marine survey fee forecasts; board resolution naming a Korean-resident compliance contact; and a written undertaking that no bearer shares or nominee arrangements exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment routing inventory includes a third-country digital money service and peer-to-peer wire, which suggests unlicensed money transmission and potential layering of insurance claim proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy requiring SWIFT MT103 through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank; original engagement contract or marine claims instruction from the underwriter; sample invoices and payment schedules; a letter from the foreign underwriter confirming that its wire originates from a licensed bank; certification that neither Wise nor any unlicensed EMI will receive corporate funds; and a draft internal AML manual demonstrating transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine survey business creates potential exposure to sanctioned vessels, prohibited cargo, or fraudulent claim indemnification, triggering targeted sanctions and insurance fraud red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete client list with foreign underwriter and insurer names and countries of incorporation; UN, OFAC, EU, and UK sanctions screening reports for every vessel IMO number, owner, and registered flag; certificate of professional marine insurance surveyor qualification; professional indemnity insurance policy; survey engagement terms excluding sanctioned jurisdictions and cargo; geographic risk matrix designed to block North Korean, Iranian, Russian, and Syrian exposures; and claim files for recent inspections if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound shareholder capital from an offshore jurisdiction exceeds the equity declared to local authorities, raising source-of-funds and over-valuation concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment notification filed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance or Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, as applicable; capital transaction declaration accepted by a licensed Korean bank; SWIFT MT103 copy from the sending bank; inward remittance certificate issued by the Korean receiving bank; bank-to-bank source-of-funds confirmation; audited or accountant-reviewed projected financials; shareholder board resolution approving the capital injection amount; declaration that paid-in capital will be used only for working capital of the Korean marine survey operation; and Korean corporate tax compliance certificate if in existence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inward capital must be sent from the overseas investor's licensed bank to the Korean LLC's designated foreign currency account at a licensed Korean bank. The remittance should be executed as a SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary being the LLC, a clear shareholder-loan or equity-investment reference, and the Korean foreign exchange transaction purpose code approved by the receiving bank. Upon receipt, the Korean bank will credit the capital account, issue an inward remittance certificate, and verify the contribution against the filed foreign investment notification or capital transaction declaration. KRW conversion is then executed onshore at market rate through a bank FX desk. No statutory minimum capital exists, so formal CPA capital verification is not mandatory, but the bank-issued capital remittance certificate should be retained for KOTRA, audits, and future dividend repatriation. All SWIFT copies and bank confirmations must be kept in the treasury file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound fee disbursements to foreign underwriters, shipowners, surveyors, reinsurers, and inspection equipment suppliers should use SWIFT MT103 for direct service payments and claims reimbursements. Commercial Letters of Credit are appropriate for purchases of calibration devices, drones, and safety equipment requiring trade settlement; Documentary Collections, both D/P and D/A, with carrier documents can be used for consignment shipments and equipment moves. Every outbound remittance must be supported by an underlying invoice, contract, and the correct Korean foreign exchange purpose code; the bank will report the payment through the Foreign Exchange Information Network and any payment to a sanctioned vessel or owner must be blocked. The underwriter wire from the client's target rails should be executed as a normal SWIFT MT103 wire from the underwriter's own licensed bank, not as a fintech peer-to-peer transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW forward contracts with licensed Korean banks for documented trade and service exposure
KRW/USD FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for underlying trade, insurance fee, and equity cash-flow hedging
Offshore KRW non-deliverable forwards available to non-resident counterparties; resident entities require bank approval and documented underlying exposure
Zero-cost participating forwards and currency options when used for commercial hedging with a relationship bank and supported by actual marine survey contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular general meeting of members approving the annual financial statements, auditor report, and discharge of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book at the registered office; open to inspection and enforcement by the National Tax Service, Financial Supervisory Service, competent District Court registration office, and members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the statutory fiscal year-end for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act; February 28 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No public filing fee; failure to convene or to approve financial statements is an administrative violation, exposes the representative member to sanctions, weakens director limitation-of-liability defenses, and can trigger registry inspection or enforcement action but not an automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for the closed fiscal year, including tax reconciliation schedules and audited financial statements if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the end of each business year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file surtax of 20% of the deficient tax; under-reporting surtax of 10-20% of evaded tax; unpaid-tax interest of 0.03% per day; persistent delinquency leads to tax seizure, enforcement, and cancellation or closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local income tax return (local portion of corporate income tax, commonly 10% of corporate income tax due)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax jurisdiction of the LLC's head office, e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government or the competent Si-Gun-Gu local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; within one month after the corporate income tax filing deadline for other fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local income tax negligence surtax of 10% of unpaid tax; daily overdue interest of 0.03% from the due date; compulsory local tax collection through seizure and eventual cancellation of the business registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax preliminary and final returns covering the semi-annual VAT tax periods with quarterly advance reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary VAT returns: April 25 (January-March) and October 25 (July-September); final VAT returns: July 25 (April-June) and January 25 (October-December); if the statutory date falls on a holiday, the due date is the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 20% of unpaid VAT; tax invoice violation penalties of 0.5-2% of supply value; daily overdue interest of 0.03% per day; habitual non-filing can trigger forced closure of the place of business and cancellation of registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly payroll withholding tax remittance and annual wage-and-income tax settlement for Korean employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding remittance by the 10th day of the following month; annual year-end payroll settlement by March 10 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold or remit triggers an additional tax of 10% of the unremitted amount plus daily overdue interest of 0.03%; repeated violations can result in tax enforcement, remedies under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, and suspension or cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual status report and, as applicable, 30-day change report for foreign investment ownership or capital changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance and Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) foreign investment one-stop window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 following the end of each foreign-invested business year; any change in foreign ownership, capital, or investment status must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative negligence fine of up to KRW 2,000,000 under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; loss of foreign-invested enterprise status and forfeiture of applicable investment incentive benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent CPA external audit report and submission to the financial supervisor, only when the statutory audit threshold is crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service of South Korea (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be approved at the regular general meeting no later than February 28 for a December year-end; the external auditor must file the signed audit report with FSS no later than two weeks after issuance or the statutory deadline for submission, whichever first requires it
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or submit the audit report triggers administrative fines under the Korean External Audit Act, discipline against the responsible directors, rejection of the financial statements for statutory purposes, and criminal or administrative enforcement by the Financial Services Commission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is legally required to appoint an independent certified public accountant under the Korean External Audit Act if, at the end of the fiscal year, total assets on the balance sheet prepared under K-IFRS are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million). A mandatory group audit may also be triggered when the consolidated total assets of the LLC and its controlled subsidiaries reach the same threshold. There is no separate turnover-only or headcount-only mandatory audit trigger for an ordinary non-listed LLC; however, a marine insurance surveyor may be contractually required by underwriters or by a governing license condition to maintain an independently reviewed or audited financial statement even if the legal threshold is not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for entities required to undergo the statutory external audit; Korean GAAP or General Corporate Accounting Standards for non-public small and medium-sized entities not subject to the mandatory external audit, with standards established by the Korean Accounting Standards Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a separate annual UBO return on every LLC. The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a current member register that accurately identifies the ultimate beneficial owners. A transfer of a membership interest in an LLC requires approval of the general meeting of members unless the articles of incorporation provide otherwise, and the transferee must be entered in the member register before the transfer can be asserted against third parties. For a foreign-owned entity, any change in ownership percentage or foreign investment status must be reported to KOTRA or the Ministry of Economy and Finance within 30 days of the change. The annual confirmation protocol is satisfied by presenting and updating the member register at each regular general meeting, recording any ownership changes in the meeting minutes, and updating the register immediately after each transferred interest; no national UBO filing fee is applicable.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,800 per year for a professional registered office or corporate secretarial agent in Seoul or Busan, including Korean-language statutory mailbox and regulatory correspondence handling; USD 250 - USD 700 per year for a simple mail-forwarding or remote provincial address arrangement.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 for a full mandatory CPA audit by a Korean registered accounting firm when the KRW 12 billion asset threshold is met; USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 for an agreed-upon procedures or limited statutory review engagement when the LLC remains below the mandatory audit threshold.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national corporate income tax (CIT) plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the CIT, yielding a combined top marginal rate of 27.5%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No marine-surveyor specific tax holiday. General regimes: R&D tax credit under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (up to 50% of qualifying R&D); foreign investment incentives for designated Free Economic Zones (e.g., Incheon FEZ); no patent box regime applicable to marine insurance surveying services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (法人税法 제60조) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; semi-annual prepayment returns for the first six months are due separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return due within 3 months of the fiscal year end (calendar-year entities: March 31); one-month extension available with NTS approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, business registration number, corporate TIN, address of domestic place of business, fiscal year-end, and representative name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa must use the Korean corporate registration number (사업자등록번호) issued to the domestic office; omission of the non-resident parent's details or local agent details can block e-filing and trigger a 20% unregistered business penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial net income per Korean GAAP adjusted by adding non-deductible expenses, deducting tax-exempt items, applying tax loss carryforwards, and adding transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Korean-source marine survey and cargo inspection fees received by the domestic entity must be included; intercompany fee adjustments under the International Tax Adjustment Act must be reflected even if no Korean tax is ultimately due; foreign-source income allocated to a Korean permanent establishment cannot be excluded without OECD-compliant attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Progressive national CIT: 10% on income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on KRW 200 million–20 billion; 22% on KRW 20–300 billion; 25% above KRW 300 billion; local income tax surcharge added at 10% of CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity is a branch of a foreign insurer, the after-tax profits remitted abroad are subject to an additional 20% branch remittance tax (plus local surcharge) under the Corporate Income Tax Act unless a tax treaty reduces or eliminates that charge; the remittance must be separately declared on the CIT return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 33 / Foreign Tax Credits and Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign income tax paid on foreign-source income, dividend-received deductions, and withholding tax credits on foreign investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean residents may claim a foreign tax credit limited to the Korean tax attributable to that foreign income; non-resident shareholders should not confuse this credit with treaty withholding relief, which is handled at the remittance stage by the withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory schedule detailing all cross-border transactions with related parties: amounts, nature, applied transfer pricing method, and contemporaneous documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be completed even where no adjustment is proposed; transactions with the overseas marine underwriting affiliates and insurance brokers must be listed by type (fees, insurance claims indemnity, IP royalties, loans). Non-filing exposes the company to a 30% surcharge under the International Tax Adjustment Act and to audit-scope widening.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 99 / Domestic Tax Representative for Non-Resident Company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of a Korean tax agent responsible for signing and receiving service of process for all NTS notifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign LLC holding Korean marine surveyor business must designate a resident director or a licensed tax agent; failure to do so permits NTS to issue deficiencies to the local agent and may result in denial of treaty claim forms.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: additive tax of 20% of the underpaid tax; under-reporting of taxable income: 10% of the underpaid amount; fraudulent under-reporting: 40%; failure to pay taxes when due: 0.022% daily overdue interest (roughly 8% annual rate). Criminal tax evasion subject to imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; aggravated penalties apply for amounts exceeding KRW 5 billion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national WHT (aggregate 22%); the rate may be reduced under an applicable bilateral DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident parent must submit, before each payment, the Korean 'Application for Income Exemption/Reduction' form to the withholding agent (and via HomeTax); provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the treaty partner's tax authority confirming residence; deliver a Beneficial Ownership Statement evidencing that the ultimate recipient is not a hybrid or conduit entity; submit shareholding records if the treaty permits a lower rate for substantial shareholders; and retain the full file for NTS inspection. Claims are ex-ante: if relief is not applied at source, a later refund application can be made within three years, but the benefit is commonly denied if beneficial ownership is not adequately evidenced.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT on cross-border interest and royalties is 20% each (plus 10% local surcharge = 22% aggregate). Under the OECD-pattern DTA applicable to Korean residents, interest is usually reduced to 10% and royalties to 10%; a specific treaty may set 5% on financial institution interest and may preserve a full source tax for Australian, Brazilian, or other non-treaty counterparties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion in foreign-related intercompany transactions triggers full Local File and Master File documentation obligations; a simplified transfer pricing disclosure may still be required for transactions above KRW 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); substance is enforced through the General Anti-Abuse Rule under the National Tax Basic Law (Art. 14-3), CFC rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act (Arts. 17–22), and the beneficial ownership condition in treaty relief. A Korean marine insurance surveyor LLC must have actual employees, office facilities, and decision-making on core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea; paper-only arrangements are disregarded and profits are reattributed to the board in Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of marine survey service revenue received through offshore underwriter wires and creation of false deductible invoices via a shell subcontractor in a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additive tax of 40% of the evaded national and local income tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes (Art. 47-3); criminal sanction under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (Art. 9) with imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine up to twice the evaded tax, aggravated to 3 years when the evaded tax exceeds KRW 5 billion; local surcharge penalties under the Local Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If a court pierces the corporate veil, directors are jointly and severally liable for the full evaded tax amount and penalties; criminal conviction additionally triggers personal asset seizure and an overseas travel ban under the NTS delinquency blacklist program.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Outbound Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to the non-resident parent without withholding the 20% national dividend WHT and the 2% local income tax surcharge, and failing timely remit the withheld amounts to the NTS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agent is liable for the unwithheld tax; additive tax of 20% of the under-withheld amount after 3 months, plus 0.022% per-day overdue interest; intentional failure may become tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and other statutory withholding officers bear personal, joint liability for the full unwithheld national and local taxes (Corporate Income Tax Act Art. 127-5; Local Tax Act Art. 103-22-2); NTS can attach personal bank accounts and real estate, and the individual may be blacklisted and barred from overseas departure until the debt is secured.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Thin Shell Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting all marine claim survey services with a wholly owned Cayman intangible holder at below arm's-length fees, operating with zero employees and no local decision-making, and failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File or file the International Tax Adjustment Act schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unilateral TP re-assessment under the arm's-length principle; 10% under-reporting surcharge; 30% penalty for failure to submit or providing international transaction documentation under International Tax Adjustment Act (Art. 11-5); automatic audit of all Korean-source activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Although a genuine TP miscalculation alone is an administrative issue, an intentionally false TP documentation used for tax evasion exposes directors to civil fraud compensation claims, disqualification from serving as directors, and criminal liability if book entries are forged; exit bans under the overseas travel restriction notice apply for unpaid reassessed taxes.
